nodes.label: Enlargement (Dilation) with Gi...

nodes.label: Scale Factor of Enlargement (k...
nodes.title: The multiplier that determines how lengths change under dilation; 0<k<1 reduces size, k>1 increases size, often taken as rational.

nodes.label: Centre of Enlargement
nodes.title: The fixed point from which all points are expanded or contracted during a dilation; corresponding points lie on rays from this centre.

nodes.label: Area Scaling under Enlargement

nodes.label: Translation of Points and Figu...

nodes.label: Axial Symmetry (Reflection acr...
nodes.title: Reflecting a figure over a given line (axis) to produce a mirror image; preserves distances and angles but reverses orientation.

nodes.label: Rotation about a Point

nodes.label: Central Symmetry (Point Reflec...

nodes.label: Axis of Symmetry Identificatio...

nodes.label: Mathematical Proof
nodes.title: A logically structured argument that establishes the truth of a mathematical statement from axioms and previously proven results.

nodes.label: Theorem
nodes.title: A mathematical statement that has been proven to be true using deductive reasoning.

nodes.label: Axiom (Postulate)
nodes.title: A foundational assumption accepted without proof that serves as a starting point for deducing other truths.

nodes.label: Deductive Reasoning
nodes.title: Deriving specific conclusions from general principles or axioms using valid logical steps.

nodes.label: Logical Implication (Implies)
nodes.title: The conditional relationship P ⇒ Q, meaning if P is true then Q must be true.

nodes.label: Converse of a Statement
nodes.title: For a conditional P ⇒ Q, the converse is Q ⇒ P and may have a different truth value.

nodes.label: Logical Equivalence (Is Equiva...
nodes.title: Two statements are logically equivalent if they always have the same truth value.

nodes.label: Biconditional (If and Only If)
nodes.title: The statement P ⇔ Q meaning both P ⇒ Q and Q ⇒ P hold; expresses an equivalence.

nodes.label: Proof by Contradiction
nodes.title: A proof technique where the negation of the desired statement is assumed and a contradiction is derived.

nodes.label: Corollary
nodes.title: A result that follows readily from a previously proven theorem with little additional argument.

nodes.label: Slope of a Line
nodes.title: Measure of a line's steepness; computed from two points or from a linear equation and used to compare line directions.

nodes.label: Parallel Lines via Slope
nodes.title: Using equal slopes to determine that two non-coincident lines are parallel.

nodes.label: Perpendicular Lines via Slope
nodes.title: Using the negative reciprocal slope condition (m1·m2 = -1) to establish that two lines are perpendicular.

nodes.label: Angle Between Two Lines
nodes.title: Finding the acute angle between lines using slope formula tanθ = |(m2 − m1)/(1 + m1m2)|.

nodes.label: Standard Form of a Linear Equa...

nodes.label: Circle Equation in Center–Radi...
